description: Canonical Token wire payload, served by the conformance test in every SDK. The numeric fields are chosen to be values that a naive float-parsing client corrupts: if an SDK ever starts parsing these into a double, its conformance test fails.

marketcap.why: 20 significant digits. Parsed as a double it rounds to 30000, which is exactly the graduation threshold — a float client would report a token as graduated one wei of market cap early.

price.why: 1 wei expressed in whole units. Survives f64 as a magnitude but not in sums; kept as a string so downstream big-decimal math starts from the exact figure.

ethPrice.why: 21 significant digits, trailing zero included. A float round-trip drops the trailing zero and the last three digits.

volume.why: 2^53 + 1, the smallest integer an IEEE-754 double cannot represent. Parsed as a double it becomes 9007199254740992.

score.why: The canonical 0.1 + 0.2 artifact. If it round-trips unchanged the value was never a double.

virtualEthAmount.why: 1 BNB in wei. Exact in f64, included so a passing test is not purely a curiosity of extreme values.

virtualTokenAmount.why: uint256 max. 78 digits, far beyond both f64 and int64.

must_be_null.why: null means unknown or absent, never zero and never the empty string. pairAddress in particular is null for every token still on the bonding curve: rendering it as 0x0 would send a caller looking for a DEX pool that does not exist.
